driving","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 - Confusables and KG hints, Chapter Eight Defensive driving

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A02
Aggressive driving breaks traffic safety laws while road rage breaks criminal laws, so the same tailgate or chase counts as a violation until the driver means harm or violence. [A02]
Why it matters: group aggression; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec08-F04, sec08-F07 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=46]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A03
Where no speed limit is posted, drive no faster than fifty-five miles per hour, whereas New York City defaults to twenty-five miles per hour unless another limit is posted, and even driving below a posted limit on a slippery or fogged road can draw a ticket for speed not reasonable for conditions [A03].
Why it matters: group speed; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec08-F09 [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A03
Use the two-second rule for a normal following cushion, and increase that count to at least three or four seconds in bad weather or when following large trucks [A03].
Why it matters: group space; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec08-F10 [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=47]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A04
Seats serve under-fours rear-facing to two, boosters serve four-to-sevens, and belts serve eight-to-fifteens, with the height-weight swap letting big young riders belt and small older riders stay seated. [A04]
Why it matters: group restraints; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec08-F13, sec08-F14 [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=48]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A08
A first handheld call costs money plus five points while first texting costs money only, then texts escalate by offense count and junior licenses suspend for either. [A08]
Why it matters: group devices; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec08-F22 [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=52]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A06
Drivers approaching a roundabout must yield at entry, look left because circulating traffic has the right-of-way, and wait for an adequate gap before entering [A06].
Why it matters: group roundabouts; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec08-F18 [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=50]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A07
Once inside, the driver gains priority and signals right to leave, while pedestrians keep crossings and splitter refuges and riders choose vehicle flow or dismounted walking. [A07]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec08-F19 [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=51]
